source.text: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Job and said:

en.L: And Job answered and said:
en.B: Then Job answered:
en.R: Then Job said:

decisions.choice: answered and said: Job replies to Zophar and to all three friends
decisions.reason: Job's answer runs through chapters 12-14, his longest speech so far. He speaks to the three friends together (verse 2 uses the plural "you") and then turns to God (13:20). The introduction stays prose.

decisions.choice: answered (Balanced), said (Readable), without "and said"
decisions.reason: Hebrew introduces speech with two verbs, "answered and said". Literal keeps both; Balanced and Readable say it once, with the same wording at every speech introduction in Job.

source.text: אָ֭מְנָם כִּ֣י אַתֶּם־עָ֑ם וְ֝עִמָּכֶ֗ם תָּמ֥וּת חָכְמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Truly indeed you [are the] people, and with you will die wisdom.

en.L: Truly you [are] the people, \q and with you wisdom will die!
en.B: No doubt you are the people who matter, \q and wisdom will die with you!
en.R: You think you are the only people who know anything, \q and that wisdom will die when you die!

decisions.choice: you are the people: biting irony, you are the only people who count
decisions.reason: Job does not mean it. "Truly" sets up the sarcasm: the friends speak as if all wisdom were theirs. The "you" is plural; Job answers all three friends.

decisions.choice: wisdom will die with you: when you are gone no one wise will be left
decisions.reason: The second line carries the irony further. Job will show in verse 3 that he knows as much as they do.

decisions.choice: the people who matter
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "who matter" so that the sarcasm of "you are the people" is heard in English (m1).

decisions.choice: You think you are the only people who know anything
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the sarcasm means, so a reader does not take it as praise (m1).

source.text: גַּם־לִ֤י לֵבָ֨ב׀כְּֽמוֹכֶ֗ם לֹא־נֹפֵ֣ל אָנֹכִ֣י מִכֶּ֑ם וְאֶת־מִי־אֵ֥ין כְּמוֹ־אֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Also to me [is] a heart like you; not falling [am] I more than you; and with whom [are] not [things] like these?

en.L: I also have a heart as well as you; \q I am not falling below you. \q And who does not [know things] like these?
en.B: But I have a mind as well as you; \q I am not inferior to you. \q Who does not know such things?
en.R: But I can think as well as you can. \q I am not less wise than you are. \q Everyone knows the things you have said!

decisions.choice: heart: mind, understanding
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where a person thinks and understands (11:12; 34:10).

decisions.choice: not falling below you: not inferior to you
decisions.reason: To "fall" from someone is to be less than they are. Job says the same again in 13:2.

decisions.choice: who does not have things like these: everyone knows what you have said
decisions.reason: "With whom are there not ..." means "who does not know ...". The friends' teaching that God is great and punishes evil is common knowledge.

decisions.choice: know
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "with whom are there not things like these" is filled out with "know", bracketed at Literal (m3).

source.text: שְׂחֹ֤ק לְרֵעֵ֨הוּ׀אֶֽהְיֶ֗ה קֹרֵ֣א לֶ֭אֱלוֹהַּ וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֑הוּ שְׂ֝ח֗וֹק צַדִּ֥יק תָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: A laughingstock to his friend I am, [one] calling to God and he answered him; a laughingstock [is the] righteous, blameless [man].

en.L: A laughingstock to his friend I am, \q one who called to God and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered him; \q a laughingstock, the righteous [and] blameless [man]!
en.B: I have become a laughingstock to my friends, \q I who called on God and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me; \q a righteous and blameless man is laughed at!
en.R: My friends laugh at me, \q even though I prayed to God and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me. \q They laugh at a man who is good and blameless.

decisions.choice: his friend ... answered him: Job speaks of himself as "one" who is mocked
decisions.reason: Job begins with "I" and goes on in the third person, as if describing anyone in his place. "Friend" is singular but stands for his friends as a group.

decisions.choice: called to God and he answered him: Job once prayed and was heard
alternatives: one who calls to God, hoping he will answer
decisions.reason: Being answered by God was a sign of his favor. The man God once answered has become a joke. The verb "answered" is in a past form.

decisions.choice: righteous and blameless: the words used of Job at the start of the book
decisions.reason: "Blameless" is the book's word for Job (1:1, 8; 2:3). The man God himself called blameless is the one people now laugh at.

decisions.choice: my friends ... me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the first person throughout, as English would (m1).

source.text: לַפִּ֣יד בּ֭וּז לְעַשְׁתּ֣וּת שַׁאֲנָ֑ן נָ֝כ֗וֹן לְמ֣וֹעֲדֵי רָֽגֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: For disaster, contempt, in [the] thought of [one] at ease; ready for [those] slipping of foot.

en.L: For disaster, contempt, in the thinking of [one] at ease; \q [it is] ready for [those whose] foot slips.
en.B: Those at ease look with contempt on disaster; \q they think it is ready for those whose feet are slipping.
en.R: People who have an easy life look down on those in trouble. \q They think trouble is waiting for anyone who slips.

decisions.choice: contempt for disaster: those who are comfortable despise people in trouble
alternatives: a torch despised (dividing the letters as one word, lappid)
decisions.reason: The first word most likely means disaster or ruin (30:24; 31:29). Read as one word with the letter before it, it would mean "a torch", which gives the older rendering "a lamp despised". The verse is hard; Job's point is that the comfortable look down on the suffering, as his friends do on him.

decisions.choice: ready: disaster stands ready for those who slip
alternatives: a blow (from a root meaning to strike)
decisions.reason: The word usually means firm or ready. Those at ease think that a fall is waiting for anyone whose foot is already slipping, so they deserve it.

decisions.choice: they think
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make "the one at ease" the subject and say what he thinks.

source.text: יִשְׁלָ֤יוּ אֹֽהָלִ֨ים׀לְשֹׁ֥דְדִ֗ים וּֽ֭בַטֻּחוֹת לְמַרְגִּ֣יזֵי אֵ֑ל לַאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵבִ֖יא אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: At peace are [the] tents of destroyers, and security [is] to [those] provoking God, to [him] who brings God in his hand.

en.L: The tents of destroyers are at peace, \q and [there is] security for those who provoke God, \q for [the one] who brings [his] god in his hand.
en.B: The tents of robbers are at peace, \q and those who provoke God are secure, \q those who carry their god in their hands.
en.R: Robbers live in peace in their homes. \q People who make God angry are safe. \q Their own strength is their god.

decisions.choice: destroyers: those who plunder and lay waste
decisions.reason: The word means people who destroy or plunder, robbers and raiders. Job answers Zophar's claim that the wicked have no escape (11:20): in fact they live at peace.

decisions.choice: provoke God: stir God to anger
decisions.reason: The verb means to make tremble or stir up, here to provoke God's anger by what they do. Yet they live securely.

decisions.choice: who bring their god in their hand: whose own power is their god
alternatives: those whom God has brought into his power
those to whom God brings plenty with his hand
decisions.reason: The line is unclear. Most likely it means people who trust their own strength or weapons as their god (compare Habakkuk 1:11). It can also be read "whom God holds in his hand", that is, whom God himself provides for.

decisions.choice: robbers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use an everyday word for those who plunder (m1).

source.text: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁאַל־נָ֣א בְהֵמ֣וֹת וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וְע֥וֹף הַ֝שָּׁמַ֗יִם וְיַגֶּד־לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: But ask, please, [the] beasts, and it will teach you, and [the] birds of the heavens, and it will tell you;

en.L: But ask now the beasts, and they will teach you, \q and the birds of the heavens, and they will tell you;
en.B: But ask the animals, and they will teach you; \q ask the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
en.R: Go and ask the animals; they will teach you. \q Ask the birds, and they will tell you.

decisions.choice: you: singular, addressed to one friend, or to each of them
decisions.reason: In verses 7-8 "you" is singular, while verses 2-3 used the plural. Job may turn to Zophar, or to each friend in turn.

decisions.choice: beasts, birds, earth, fish: all the realms of living things
decisions.reason: Animals, birds, the earth and the fish of the sea (verse 8) are the creatures named in Genesis 1:26-28. All of them, Job says, can teach the friends what they think is their own special wisdom (verse 9).

source.text: א֤וֹ שִׂ֣יחַ לָאָ֣רֶץ וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ לְ֝ךָ֗ דְּגֵ֣י הַיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, and will recount to you [the] fish of the sea.

en.L: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, \q and the fish of the sea will recount [it] to you.
en.B: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, \q and the fish of the sea will declare it to you.
en.R: Or talk to the earth, and it will teach you. \q Even the fish in the sea will tell you.

decisions.choice: speak to: talk with
alternatives: the shrubs of the earth (a noun spelled with the same letters)
decisions.reason: The word is most likely the verb "talk" or "muse". Spelled the same, a noun means a shrub, which would add the plants to the creatures of verse 7.

decisions.choice: recount: tell in order, declare
decisions.reason: The verb (safar) means to count and so to tell over, to declare (Psalm 19:2).

source.text: מִ֭י לֹא־יָדַ֣ע בְּכָל־אֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֥י יַד־יְ֝הוָה עָ֣שְׂתָה זֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: Who does not know among all these that [the] hand of YHWH has done this?

en.L: Who among all these does not know \q that the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done this?
en.B: Which of all these does not know \q that the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done this?
en.R: Every one of these creatures knows \q that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} has done this.

decisions.choice: YHWH: the divine name, here alone in the speeches of Job
alternatives: God (Eloah), the reading of some Hebrew manuscripts
decisions.reason: The book uses the name YHWH in its prose frame and in the introductions to God's speeches (38:1; 40:1, 3, 6; 42:1), but in the speeches themselves only here. Some Hebrew manuscripts read Eloah, the word for God used throughout the poem. The words match Isaiah 41:20, "the hand of the LORD has done this", and may be a saying Job quotes.

decisions.choice: this: all that has been described, the way the world is ordered
decisions.reason: "This" points to the world as Job has just described it, where the violent are at peace (verse 6), and to God's rule over every life (verse 10).

decisions.choice: who does not know: everyone knows
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer that every creature knows it.

decisions.choice: Every one of these creatures knows
alternatives: Who among all these does not know?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies (m3), and says "himself" for "the hand of".

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ֭יָדוֹ נֶ֣פֶשׁ כָּל־חָ֑י וְ֝ר֗וּחַ כָּל־בְּשַׂר־אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: In whose hand [is the] life of every living thing, and [the] breath of all flesh of man.

en.L: In whose hand [is the] life of every living thing, \q and the breath of all human flesh.
en.B: In {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand is the life of every living creature \q and the breath of every human being.
en.R: God holds the life of every creature in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q and the breath of every person.

decisions.choice: life: the living being, its very life
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) means the life of a living creature, not a part of it separate from the body.

decisions.choice: breath: the breath of life
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) can mean wind, breath or spirit. Here, beside "life", it is the breath that keeps people alive (Genesis 6:17; Job 27:3). God gives it and can take it back (34:14-15).

decisions.choice: all flesh of man: every human being
decisions.reason: "Flesh" is the human body, and the word for man here means humankind. The first line speaks of every creature, the second of every human.

decisions.choice: In his hand (B); God holds ... in his hand (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence instead of continuing the question of verse 9; Readable names God.

source.text: הֲלֹא־אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן וְ֝חֵ֗ךְ אֹ֣כֶל יִטְעַם־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Does] not [the] ear test words, and [the] palate taste food for itself?

en.L: Does not the ear test words, \q as the palate tastes food for itself?
en.B: Does not the ear test words \q as the tongue tastes food?
en.R: The ear tests what it hears, \q just as the tongue tastes food.

decisions.choice: the ear tests words: a person can judge for himself what he hears
decisions.reason: This sounds like a common saying; Elihu uses it too (34:3). Job means that he can weigh his friends' words himself and need not accept them because they are old wisdom (verse 12).

decisions.choice: palate: the roof of the mouth, used for taste
decisions.reason: The palate is where food is tasted; the line pictures the mouth testing food.

decisions.choice: tongue
decisions.reason: English says the tongue tastes food (m2); Literal keeps "palate".

source.text: בִּֽישִׁישִׁ֥ים חָכְמָ֑ה וְאֹ֖רֶךְ יָמִ֣ים תְּבוּנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: With aged [ones is] wisdom, and length of days [is] understanding.

en.L: With the aged [is] wisdom, \q and length of days [is] understanding.
en.B: Wisdom is with the aged, \q and long life brings understanding.
en.R: Old people are wise, \q and those who have lived long understand much.

decisions.choice: a statement, likely the friends' claim that Job quotes in order to answer it
alternatives: a question: is wisdom with the aged?
decisions.reason: Bildad appealed to the wisdom of past generations (8:8-10). Job may be quoting that view, to answer in verse 13 that true wisdom belongs to God. It can also be read as a question expecting the answer no.

decisions.choice: the aged: the very old
decisions.reason: The word is rare and means the very old (15:10; 29:8; 32:6).

source.text: עִ֭מּוֹ חָכְמָ֣ה וּגְבוּרָ֑ה ל֝֗וֹ עֵצָ֥ה וּתְבוּנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: With him [are] wisdom and might; to him [belong] counsel and understanding.

en.L: With {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [are] wisdom and might; \q to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [belong] counsel and understanding.
en.B: With God are wisdom and might; \q counsel and understanding are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}.
en.R: God is the one who has real wisdom and power. \q He knows what to do and understands everything.

decisions.choice: with him: with God, set against "with the aged" in verse 12
decisions.reason: "Him" is God, the one whose hand holds all life (verses 9-10). Verse 12 said wisdom is with the old; verse 13 says that real wisdom and power belong to God.

decisions.choice: wisdom, might, counsel, understanding: the gifts of a ruler
decisions.reason: The same four words come together in Isaiah 11:2 for the Spirit resting on the coming king. Job lists them to say that God rules, as verses 14-25 go on to show.

decisions.choice: counsel: the power to plan and decide
decisions.reason: The word ('etsah) means advice, and so the ability to make plans and carry them out (Proverbs 19:21).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, so the contrast with verse 12 is clear (m1).

source.text: הֵ֣ן יַ֭הֲרוֹס וְלֹ֣א יִבָּנֶ֑ה יִסְגֹּ֥ר עַל־אִ֝֗ישׁ וְלֹ֣א יִפָּתֵֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, he tears down, and it will not be rebuilt; he shuts on a man, and it will not be opened.

en.L: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tears down, and it will not be rebuilt; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shuts [a door] on {{gender:a person|a man}}, and it will not be opened.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} tears down, it cannot be rebuilt; \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shuts someone in, no one can open it.
en.R: When God tears something down, no one can build it again. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} locks someone up, no one can set them free.

decisions.choice: look: a word that draws attention, here bringing in a picture of what God does
decisions.reason: The word (hen) means "look" or "see". Verses 14-15 describe what happens whenever God acts, so Balanced and Readable say "when".

decisions.choice: shuts in: imprisons; Job takes up the verb Zophar used
decisions.reason: Zophar said God shuts up the guilty (11:10). Job agrees that no one can undo what God does, but his point is God's sheer power, not his justice. Job said God had hedged him in (3:23).

decisions.choice: {{gender:a person|a man}}
decisions.reason: The word means anyone, so the gender setting gives "a person" by default.

source.text: הֵ֤ן יַעְצֹ֣ר בַּמַּ֣יִם וְיִבָ֑שׁוּ וִֽ֝ישַׁלְּחֵ֗ם וְיַ֖הַפְכוּ אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, he holds back the waters, and they dry up; and he sends them out, and they overturn [the] earth.

en.L: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} holds back the waters, and they dry up; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends them out, and they overturn the earth.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} holds back the waters, they dry up; \q when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lets them loose, they overwhelm the land.
en.R: When God holds back the rain, everything dries up. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends a flood, it destroys the land.

decisions.choice: holds back the waters: drought, when no rain falls
decisions.reason: God "shuts up the heavens" so there is no rain (Deuteronomy 11:17; 1 Kings 8:35).

decisions.choice: sends them out: flood that overturns the land
decisions.reason: Let loose, the same waters destroy. A reader may think of the flood in Noah's day (Genesis 7). Both drought and flood come from God's hand.

decisions.choice: the rain ... a flood
decisions.reason: Readable names the two disasters the waters bring (m1, m2).

source.text: עִ֭מּוֹ עֹ֣ז וְתֽוּשִׁיָּ֑הל֝֗וֹ שֹׁגֵ֥ג וּמַשְׁגֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: With him [are] strength and sound wisdom; to him [belong one] going astray and [one] leading astray.

en.L: With {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [are] strength and sound wisdom; \q to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [belong the one] who strays and [the one] who leads astray.
en.B: With {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} are strength and true wisdom; \q the misled and the misleader are both {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}.
en.R: God is strong and wise in all {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does. \q He rules over people who are fooled and people who fool them.

decisions.choice: sound wisdom: wisdom that works and succeeds
decisions.reason: The word (tushiyyah) means practical wisdom that gets results (5:12; 6:13; 11:6). It echoes verse 13.

decisions.choice: both the misled and the one who misleads belong to God
decisions.reason: Even error and deceit do not escape God's rule. Job does not say that God approves of deceit, only that the deceiver and his victim are both under God's power.

decisions.choice: He rules over
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means for both to "belong" to God (m2).

source.text: מוֹלִ֣יךְ יוֹעֲצִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְֽשֹׁפְטִ֥ים יְהוֹלֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Leading away counselors stripped, and judges he makes fools.

en.L: [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] leads counselors away stripped, \q and makes fools of judges.
en.B: He leads counselors away stripped \q and makes fools of judges.
en.R: He leads wise advisers away as prisoners \q and makes judges look foolish.

decisions.choice: leading: the first of a string of descriptions of what God does
decisions.reason: Verses 17-24 are a list of things God does, most of them beginning with a participle, like a hymn of praise (compare 5:9-16). But Job's list is dark: it is all about God bringing the great low.

decisions.choice: stripped: barefoot and stripped, as captives
decisions.reason: The word (sholal) means stripped or barefoot, as prisoners of war were led away (Micah 1:8; Isaiah 20:2-4).

decisions.choice: makes fools: makes them act foolishly
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of God making fools of diviners (Isaiah 44:25).

decisions.choice: as prisoners
decisions.reason: Readable says what being led away stripped means (m2).

source.text: מוּסַ֣ר מְלָכִ֣ים פִּתֵּ֑חַ וַיֶּאְסֹ֥ר אֵ֝ז֗וֹר בְּמָתְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] bond of kings he loosens, and binds a loincloth on their waists.

en.L: [The] bond of kings {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loosens, \q and binds a loincloth on their waists.
en.B: He loosens the bonds that kings put on others \q and binds a captive's cloth around their own waists.
en.R: He frees those whom kings have put in chains, \q and makes the kings themselves prisoners.

decisions.choice: the bond of kings: the bonds kings put on their subjects and prisoners
alternatives: the belt of kings, the sign of their rank
decisions.reason: The word usually means discipline, but here it seems to come from the verb "bind". The line then means God undoes what kings have bound, and the next line binds the kings themselves. Others take it as the royal belt that God takes from them.

decisions.choice: a loincloth: the waistcloth of a captive or a slave
decisions.reason: Captives were led away in little more than a cloth around the waist (Isaiah 20:2-4). Kings who bound others are bound and led off as prisoners.

decisions.choice: the bonds that kings put on others; a captive's cloth (B); those whom kings have put in chains; prisoners (R)
alternatives: the bond of kings; a loincloth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the reading chosen in m1 and the picture in m2.

source.text: מוֹלִ֣יךְ כֹּהֲנִ֣ים שׁוֹלָ֑ל וְאֵֽתָנִ֣ים יְסַלֵּֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: Leading away priests stripped, and [the] long-established he overthrows.

en.L: [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] leads priests away stripped, \q and overthrows the long-established.
en.B: He leads priests away stripped \q and overthrows those firmly in power.
en.R: He leads priests away as prisoners \q and brings down people who seemed safe in power.

decisions.choice: priests: among the highest officials of a nation
decisions.reason: Job lists every rank of the powerful: counselors, judges, kings, priests, nobles, elders (verses 17-21). Priests were leaders in public life as well as worship.

decisions.choice: the long-established: those whose position seemed permanent
decisions.reason: The word ('etan) means lasting or ever-flowing (Psalm 74:15; Numbers 24:21). Here it means powerful people whose place seemed secure.

decisions.choice: overthrows: twists, brings to ruin
decisions.reason: The verb means to twist or overturn (Exodus 23:8; Proverbs 13:6).

source.text: מֵסִ֣יר שָׂ֭פָה לְנֶאֱמָנִ֑ים וְטַ֖עַם זְקֵנִ֣ים יִקָּֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: Removing [the] lip of [the] trusted, and [the] discernment of elders he takes away.

en.L: [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] removes the speech of the trusted, \q and takes away the discernment of elders.
en.B: He silences trusted advisers \q and takes away the judgment of elders.
en.R: He leaves trusted advisers with nothing to say, \q and he takes away the good sense of the elders.

decisions.choice: removes the lip: takes away the power to speak
decisions.reason: The lip stands for speech (11:2). God takes away the ability of trusted advisers to give counsel.

decisions.choice: the trusted: those whose words were relied on
decisions.reason: The word means trustworthy or reliable people, here advisers whose word was trusted.

decisions.choice: discernment: good judgment
decisions.reason: The word (ta'am) means taste, and so good sense and judgment (1 Samuel 25:33; Proverbs 11:22).

decisions.choice: silences
decisions.reason: Balanced says what taking away the lip means (m1).

source.text: שׁוֹפֵ֣ךְ בּ֭וּז עַל־נְדִיבִ֑ים וּמְזִ֖יחַ אֲפִיקִ֣ים רִפָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Pouring contempt on nobles, and [the] belt of [the] strong he loosens.

en.L: [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] pours contempt on nobles, \q and loosens the belt of the strong.
en.B: He pours contempt on nobles \q and loosens the belt of the mighty.
en.R: He brings shame on important people \q and takes away the strength of the powerful.

decisions.choice: pours contempt on nobles: the same words as Psalm 107:40
decisions.reason: The first line matches Psalm 107:40 word for word, and verse 24 matches the rest of that verse.

decisions.choice: loosens the belt: makes them helpless
decisions.reason: A belt was tightened for work or battle (1 Kings 20:11; Isaiah 5:27). Loosening it leaves a man unready and weak.

decisions.choice: the strong: the mighty
decisions.reason: The word is rare. Elsewhere it means stream-beds; here it is used of strong men.

decisions.choice: takes away the strength
decisions.reason: Readable says what the loosened belt means (m2).

source.text: מְגַלֶּ֣ה עֲ֭מֻקוֹת מִנִּי־חֹ֑שֶׁךְ וַיֹּצֵ֖א לָא֣וֹר צַלְמָֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: Uncovering deep things out of darkness, and brings out to light deep darkness.

en.L: [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] uncovers deep things out of darkness, \q and brings deep darkness out to light.
en.B: He reveals deep things from the darkness \q and brings the deepest darkness into the light.
en.R: He uncovers secrets hidden in the dark \q and brings the darkest places into the light.

decisions.choice: deep things: what is hidden from human sight
decisions.reason: Nothing is hidden from God (Psalm 139:11-12; Daniel 2:22). Among the acts of judgment around it, the verse may mean that God exposes the secret plans of the powerful.

decisions.choice: deep darkness: the thickest darkness
decisions.reason: The word (tsalmavet) means deep darkness. Older translations read it as "the shadow of death" (Psalm 23:4). Job used it of his birth night and of the land of the dead (3:5; 10:21-22).

source.text: מַשְׂגִּ֣יא לַ֭גּוֹיִם וַֽיְאַבְּדֵ֑ם שֹׁטֵ֥חַ לַ֝גּוֹיִ֗ם וַיַּנְחֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Making great nations and destroys them; spreading out nations and leads them.

en.L: [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] makes nations great and destroys them; \q [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] spreads nations out and leads them [away].
en.B: He makes nations great, then destroys them; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} enlarges nations, then leads them away.
en.R: He makes nations grow strong, and then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroys them. \q He makes them spread out, and then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads them away as captives.

decisions.choice: makes great ... spreads out: makes nations grow in number and land
decisions.reason: Both verbs speak of growth: a nation grows great and spreads over more land. In each line God then undoes what he gave.

decisions.choice: leads them: leads them away into exile
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to lead or guide. Set against "destroys" in the first line, it most likely means leading a nation away into captivity.

decisions.choice: as captives
decisions.reason: Readable says where they are led, following m2.

source.text: מֵסִ֗יר לֵ֭ב רָאשֵׁ֣י עַם־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם בְּתֹ֣הוּ לֹא־דָֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Removing [the] heart of [the] heads of [the] people of the earth, and makes them wander in a waste, no way.

en.L: [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] takes away the heart of the chiefs of the people of the earth, \q and makes them wander in a waste [with] no road.
en.B: He takes away the understanding of the leaders of the earth \q and makes them wander in a trackless waste.
en.R: He takes away the good sense of the world's leaders \q and leaves them lost in an empty desert with no road.

decisions.choice: heart: understanding, good sense
decisions.reason: The heart is the mind (verse 3). God takes away the leaders' ability to think and plan.

decisions.choice: the people of the earth: all the nations
decisions.reason: With "the earth" the phrase here means the peoples of the world, following the nations of verse 23.

decisions.choice: a trackless waste: the words of Psalm 107:40, with the word of Genesis 1:2
decisions.reason: "Makes them wander in a waste with no road" is the second half of Psalm 107:40 (see verse 21). The word for waste (tohu) is the "formless" of Genesis 1:2.

source.text: יְמַֽשְׁשׁוּ־חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־א֑וֹר וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם כַּשִּׁכּֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: They grope [in] darkness and no light, and he makes them wander like a drunkard.

en.L: They grope [in] darkness, and [there is] no light; \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes them stagger like a drunkard.
en.B: They grope in the dark without light, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes them stagger like drunkards.
en.R: They feel their way in the dark with no light. \q He makes them stumble around like drunk people.

decisions.choice: grope in the dark: the helplessness of the blind
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:29 warns of groping at noon like the blind in darkness. The leaders who once guided others cannot find their own way.

decisions.choice: makes them wander: the same verb as verse 24, here staggering
decisions.reason: The verb means to wander or stray. With "like a drunkard" it is the unsteady walk of a drunk man (Isaiah 19:14; Psalm 107:27).

decisions.choice: drunkards (B); drunk people (R)
decisions.reason: The singular stands for any drunk man; Balanced and Readable use the plural to match "them".
